english: For a real number $k$, consider the system of equations
Then the sum of all real values of $k$ for which this system has no solution is ______.
hindi: वास्तविक संख्या $k$ के लिए समीकरण निकाय
पर विचार कीजिए। तब $k$ के उन सभी वास्तविक मानों का योग, जिनके लिए इस निकाय का कोई हल नहीं है, ______ है।
solution: $\Delta=0\iff$ the homogeneous system has non-trivial solutions; at $k=1$ every row is a multiple of $(1,2,-1)$:
$x+2y-z=1$, $x+2y-z=\frac12$, $x+2y-z=-1$: three parallel, disjoint planes, so no solution
solution_full: For $k\ne1,-5$, $\Delta\ne0$ and Cramer's rule gives a unique solution, so these $k$ are excluded.
$\Delta=0$ is also exactly the condition for the associated homogeneous system (right-hand sides $0$) to have non-trivial solutions; we now test the two values against the given constants.
$k=1$: the equations are $x+2y-z=1$, $2(x+2y-z)=1$, $-(x+2y-z)=1$, that is $x+2y-z=1,\ \frac12,\ -1$. The three planes are parallel and pairwise disjoint, so there is no solution.

$k=-5$: the rank of the coefficient matrix is $2$ (the minor $\begin{vmatrix}-5&2\\2&-2\end{vmatrix}=6\ne0$). Replacing the first column by the constants: $\Delta_1=\begin{vmatrix}1&2&-1\\1&-2&-2\\1&-2&-5\end{vmatrix}=1(10-4)-2(-5+2)-1(-2+2)=12\ne0$.
Since $\Delta=0$ but $\Delta_1\ne0$, the system is inconsistent at $k=-5$ as well.
So the system has no solution exactly for $k=1$ and $k=-5$, and the sum is $-4$.
originality_note: New: a parameter family whose coefficient matrix is (k-1)I plus a rank-one matrix, so at the double root the three planes are parallel and disjoint and at the simple root the system fails by a non-zero Cramer determinant (way 5). Closest known: the system kx+y+z=1, x+ky+z=1, x+y+kz=1. Different because: the rank-one direction is (1,2,-1), so the parallel planes are not visible from the rows, and both singular values must be tested separately.
blueprint_concepts: Solving system of linear equations when all three planes are parallel and disjoint
Solving system of homogeneous linear equations

concept_use.Cramer's rule: For k != 1, -5 the system has a unique solution by Cramer's rule, and at k = -5 the non-zero Delta_1 shows inconsistency.
concept_use.Solving system of linear equations when: At k = 1 every equation is a multiple of x + 2y - z with right-hand sides 1, 1/2, -1: three parallel, disjoint planes.
concept_use.Solving system of homogeneous linear equ: Delta = 0 is the condition for the homogeneous system to have non-trivial solutions; it gives the two candidate values k = 1 and k = -5.

stem_review: Read as a student: k real; 'no solution' is the only condition; both singular values give no solution, so the sum is -4. Checked ranks with sympy: k = 1 rank 1 vs augmented 2; k = -5 rank 2 vs 3. Answer -4, a negative integer as planned. Changed: removed a leftover fragment from the first line of the full solution.
key_step: Factor Delta = (k-1)^2(k+5); k = 1 gives parallel disjoint planes and k = -5 gives Delta_1 != 0.
justification: Three concepts linked: singular values from the determinant, recognising rank one (parallel planes) at the double root, and a Cramer determinant test at the other; numerical answer. Comparable to 2023-P1-Q14 (L1) in topic but with two separate case checks and a factorisation, like 2026-P1-Q6 (L3).
